text:
alina: Heads-up — I want to propose a cost-aware SLO priority degradation policy for GPU scarcity events. TL;DR: automatically throttle low-priority tenants (best-effort) to preserve SLOs for paid/critical tiers and avoid runaway error-budget burn and over-provisioning costs. Thoughts? :thinking:

sam: 👍 overall makes sense. two quick concerns: (1) how do we quantify 'degradation' as an SLI so it plugs into EB reporting? (2) keep alerts quiet for transient blips.

ryan: For (1) we can emit a per-tenant "degraded_tokens" counter whenever the runtime applies a rate-limit or soft-queue overflow fallback. Then an SLI is degraded_tokens / served_tokens over a window. Example PromQL (5m window):

```
# fraction of tokens served under degradation for each tenant
sum by (tenant) (increase(redwood_inference_degraded_tokens_total[5m]))
/
sum by (tenant) (increase(redwood_inference_tokens_served_total[5m]))
```

ryan: We should also add a recording rule: `record: tenant:degraded_fraction:rate5m` to avoid expensive queries in dashboards/alerts.

jess: Product note: customers will ask if degraded tokens are billed. My proposal: for the experiment, mark degraded tokens as billable but tagged for potential credit if SLA target is missed and we took degradation action. Need legal + billing input before we make it permanent. @katie do you want to loop finance?

katie: Yes please. Finance wants a clear mapping: degraded_tokens -> potential credit policy. If we do credits, we should track them in a separate metric `degraded_tokens_creditable_total` (simple boolean tag or label).

alina: Alerting side: we don't want pager storms for small, noisy degradations. Suggested alert rule: only alert if tenant degraded_fraction > 0.02 for 10m AND error_budget_remaining_percent < 30% for that tier. That keeps burn visibility only when it's meaningful.

sam: Agree. Also add a ‘sampled SLI’ for infra-only dashboards so SREs can see fleet-level signal without per-tenant noise. Sampling approach: compute p50/p95 of degraded_fraction across top N tenants instead of alerting on each tenant.

ryan: Quick example alert pseudocode:

```
# fire when a paying tenant is both experiencing degradation and close to burning EB
alert: PayingTenantDegradation
expr: tenant:degraded_fraction:rate5m{tier=~"paid|enterprise"} > 0.02
  and tenant:error_budget_remaining_percent{tier=~"paid|enterprise"} < 30
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "{{ $labels.tenant }} degraded tokens >2% & EB <30%"
```

jess: Customer comms: add a short blurb to status page explaining queued/throttled behavior and that we're prioritizing critical traffic. Also add a toggle in Console so tenants can opt into 'best-effort' mode to save cost.

katie: Ops/finance action: run cost simulation for two scenarios: (A) autoscale to meet peak (expensive) vs (B) keep headroom and degrade best-effort tenants. We need expected monthly $ delta + estimated customer churn risk.

alina: Operational plan proposal:
- Start a 2-week experiment in us-west1 GPU pool (non-critical region)
- Instrument metrics: `redwood_inference_degraded_tokens_total`, `degraded_tokens_creditable_total`, `tenant:degraded_fraction:rate5m`
- Create Grafana dashboard with fleet-level panels + top-20 tenants by degraded_fraction
- Apply alert rules with 10m wait and EB gating as above
- If experiment stable, roll to us-east then global

ops-bot: autoscaler:policy:update applied to us-west1 test pool (scale_down_threshold=0.65, best_effort_degrade=true) — will log events to `/var/log/redwood/degrade-events.log`

sam: One more: SLO reporting. For monthly SLO dashboards we should show two rows: "Observed SLI (no-degrade mitigation)" and "Observed SLI (after degradation policy)" so stakeholders can see tradeoffs. This makes it explicit that degradation is an intentional reliability knob not a regression.

ryan: Good point. Implementation note: record both raw and post-mitigation SLIs. Eg: `tenant:slis_raw:availability` vs `tenant:slis_after_mitigation:availability`.

jess: I'll draft the customer-facing copy. Also we should prepare an FAQ for support with examples (when tenants see queued requests, what to do).

katie: I'll coordinate finance + legal for the credit policy and run the cost sims. ETA 3 business days.

alina: OK — next steps assigned. I'll open a RFC in internal docs with the PromQL, recording rules, dashboard mockups, and the experiment runbook. Thanks all. :rocket:
